target_module: origins/tools/river-carver.ts (offline authoring helper only, proposed; no runtime target)

data_fields.name: river_walk_count_per_map
data_fields.donor_constant: c = (100 - aridity/4) * r * len * len / 1000000 (integer arithmetic)

data_fields.name: runner_up_chance_max
data_fields.donor_constant: d2/(d1+d2) with 0.5 when d1 is 0; at most 0.5 by heap order (my reasoning)

best_idea: Generate a water or boundary feature by a priority-flood walk from a random start to the map edge, sometimes taking the runner-up tile with a weighted chance, then fill the basins it passes through as lakes.
decision_why: Frankendom zones are authored data on one runtime with server-verified positions; a random carver at runtime would be a second source of truth unless its seed and output were frozen into zone data, and no fight, zone or spawn ruling needs procedural rivers. At most it fits as an offline map-authoring helper, which is not a combat or zone mechanic.
acceptance: Not a play feature. If built as an offline authoring helper, a test runs the carver twice with one seed and gets identical river tiles, and asserts every river ends on a border tile or on an existing river.
